stories.head: Zelensky says treating Putin as a friend is like befriending Hitler
stories.say: Volodymyr Zelensky has called Donald Trump's description of Vladimir Putin as his friend strange, saying Putin is an aggressor and a killer who can't be a friend.
stories.stand: In a BBC interview in Kyiv, Ukraine's president urged Washington to put more pressure on Moscow.
body: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky told the BBC in Kyiv on Friday that Donald Trump's description of Vladimir Putin as "my friend" was strange, CBS News and ABC News reported.

Zelensky called Putin an aggressor and a killer, and compared the idea of friendship with him to treating Adolf Hitler as a friend during the Second World War. He urged the US to put more pressure on Russia.
Asked about it on Thursday, Trump said "We want to stop killing" and that he wants a deal. Trump had called Putin a friend at a summit in China a week earlier.

stories.head: Russian drones hit Ukraine's power and rail in nine regions
stories.say: Russia launched one hundred and fifty-five drones at Ukraine overnight into Friday, hitting power, rail and homes in nine regions. At least four people were killed.
stories.stand: Ukraine says it shot down 110 drones, but power was cut in parts of six regions.
body: Russian forces launched 155 attack drones at Ukraine from Thursday evening, 51 of them jet-powered, Euronews reported. Ukraine's air defences said they shot down 110.

Prime Minister Sergey Koretsky said railway, energy and residential targets were hit in nine regions. Two people were killed at an enterprise in Nizhyn, a woman of 86 died in Izium and one person was killed in Kryvyi Rih.
Power was cut in parts of Dnipropetrovsk, Zaporizhzhia, Kirovohrad, Sumy, Kharkiv and Kherson regions. Ukraine halted electricity exports after an earlier attack on 20 November.

stories.head: Trump says victory over Iran will come 'whenever I want'
stories.say: Donald Trump says he's giving Iran a chance to make a deal but doubts it will. Iran's navy, meanwhile, claims it retook two tankers seized by the US, without giving evidence.
stories.stand: Trump has said he will allow until the new year for a peace agreement.
body: Speaking at Mar-a-Lago on Thursday after calling US troops, President Donald Trump said victory over Iran would come "whenever I want it to be", CBS News reported. He said Iran was being given a chance to make a deal, but doubted it would take it.
Trump also played down reports that Russia and China had helped Iran target US forces. He has said he will allow until the new year for a peace agreement.

On Friday, Iran's navy commander, Rear Admiral Shahram Irani, claimed Iranian commandos had retaken two tankers seized by the US. He gave no evidence, and the US has not announced seizing any Iran-linked commercial ship since April.

stories.head: US says it disabled another ship trying to breach Iran blockade
stories.say: The US military says it disabled a Palau-flagged cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman on Thursday as it tried to breach the blockade of Iranian ports. The crew were unharmed.
stories.stand: Central Command says the Pacific Archer is at least the 15th ship disabled since the blockade began in April.
body: US Central Command said a military aircraft fired precision munitions at the stern of the Palau-flagged M/V Pacific Archer in the Gulf of Oman on Thursday, disabling its propulsion, ITV News reported, citing AP. The civilian crew were unharmed.
It is at least the 15th vessel disabled since the blockade of Iranian ports began in April, and the sixth since it resumed in July. The military says it has redirected 158 merchant ships.
Separately, defence officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey met in Islamabad on Friday under their new joint defence pact.

stories.say: Iran's foreign minister has called accusations over the drone attack in Kuwait that killed two Italian technicians baseless, and proposed a joint investigation.
stories.stand: Italy says Iranian drones hit Kuwaiti military sites; Gulf states blame Tehran.
body: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi called the accusations baseless and proposed a joint investigation with Italy and Kuwait, Euronews reported. Iran's armed forces spokesperson denied any military operation in the region.

Italy's Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani told the Senate that several Iranian drones struck Kuwaiti military facilities on Thursday. One hit an air defence radar centre where two Italian specialists working for Rheinmetall were killed.
Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Bahrain blamed Iran. Iran's embassy in Rome also rejected any role, CBS News reported.

stories.head: Strike on Saudi refinery at Jazan kills a worker
stories.say: A projectile hit an oil refinery in Jazan on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast on Thursday, killing a Nepali worker. The Saudi-led coalition blames Yemen's Houthis.
stories.stand: The fire briefly halted some operations; the Houthis had not commented.
body: An aerial projectile hit an oil refinery in Jazan, near the Yemeni border, on Thursday, Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said, causing a fire and temporarily halting some operations, Al Jazeera reported.

One worker, a Nepali national, was killed and several others were injured. The ministry did not name an attacker. The Saudi-led coalition said the Houthis were responsible and that it destroyed a launch platform in Hodeidah.
The day before, the Houthis claimed attacks on Ras Tanura and on ports in Jeddah and Jazan. The refinery can process up to 400,000 barrels of crude a day.

stories.head: Ukraine claims North Korea has paused military aid to Russia
stories.say: Ukraine's military intelligence says North Korea has suspended military aid to Russia after a diplomatic row over Seoul. Neither Moscow nor Pyongyang has confirmed it.
stories.stand: The claim comes from Ukraine's HUR intelligence agency and has not been independently verified.
body: Ukraine's military intelligence agency, HUR, says North Korea has suspended military assistance to Russia on Kim Jong Un's personal decision, Euronews reported. Neither Moscow nor Pyongyang had confirmed or denied it.

HUR says Pyongyang took offence at remarks by Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Andrei Rudenko about normalising relations with Seoul. Euronews noted that Rudenko made no public statement in the terms HUR describes.
According to HUR, the measures include a halt to KN-23 missile deliveries and artillery shells. Putin and Kim signed a mutual defence pact in June 2024.

stories.say: Aung San Suu Kyi's son, Kim Aris, has spoken to his mother for the first time in five years. He says the monitored call stayed on family matters.
stories.stand: Myanmar's military says the 81-year-old is under house arrest; Aris rejects that label.
body: Kim Aris, the son of Myanmar's detained former leader Aung San Suu Kyi, has spoken to her for the first time in five years, Euronews reported. Myanmar's embassy in London contacted the Foreign Office the week before.

Aris said the call was recorded and monitored and stayed on family matters. The military says it has moved Suu Kyi, 81, to house arrest at an undisclosed location. Aris says she has no media access and rejects the label.
He urged other countries to keep up sanctions and not to re-engage with the military, which seized power in February 2021.

stories.head: Estonia to close its border with Russia from 1 December
stories.say: Estonia will shut its border with Russia on Tuesday, the first of December. Its foreign minister says it's a response to Russian sabotage and attacks on Europe.
stories.stand: Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna announced it in Baku.
body: Estonia will close its frontier with Russia on 1 December, Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said in Baku on Friday, Euronews reported.
Tsahkna said the decision responds to growing security concerns, including more Russian sabotage and attacks targeting Europe. "We are not happy about that," he said, but Estonia needed to respond.
Estonia, which borders Russia, opened an embassy in Baku on the same day. It will co-host next year's Ukraine Recovery Conference.

stories.say: Lebanon's prime minister, Nawaf Salam, says France is preparing a UN resolution that could let peacekeepers keep some tasks after their mandate ends at the end of December.
stories.stand: About 7,500 UNIFIL troops are in southern Lebanon; the Security Council voted last year to end the mission.
body: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam told AP that a new proposal could let the UN force in southern Lebanon, UNIFIL, keep working after its mandate expires on 31 December, ITV News reported. He said France is preparing a Security Council resolution. France has not commented.
UNIFIL would keep tasks such as clearing mines and escorting aid convoys during a drawdown. US officials reportedly said Washington is open to considering it.
About 7,500 peacekeepers are stationed in southern Lebanon. The Security Council voted last year to end the mission.

stories.head: Winter rains force Gaza's displaced families to move again
stories.say: UN agencies say about one point three six million people in Gaza are living in tents or makeshift shelters, and November's storms flooded tens of thousands of tents.
stories.stand: UN estimates suggest about 226,000 people were affected by flooding that began on 6 November.
body: A storm that began on 6 November flooded about 70,000 tents within 12 hours, according to Gaza's Government Media Office, Al Jazeera reported. UN preliminary estimates put the number of people affected at about 226,000.

UN OCHA says about 1.36 million people, 65% of Gaza's population, live in tents or makeshift shelters. More than half of its 1,700 displacement sites are on flood-prone land, according to IOM and WFP.
The UN said more than 150,000 tents were waiting outside Gaza on 13 November. Israel's COGAT says nearly 100,000 have entered under its winter programme.

stories.say: Mexico's president, Claudia Sheinbaum, has called a new US tip line for reporting cartel members in Mexico clearly an act of interference.
stories.stand: DEA chief Terry Cole launched anonymous channels for tips about Sinaloa state.
body: The US Drug Enforcement Administration has opened anonymous tip lines for Mexicans to report members of criminal networks in Sinaloa state, corrupt officials and money launderers, CBS News reported. DEA Administrator Terry Cole announced them on X.
President Claudia Sheinbaum called the move "clearly an act of interference" on Thursday and said the DEA has plenty of work to do in its own country.
Sheinbaum says security cooperation with Washington will continue, but without subordination. The DEA did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

stories.head: Venezuela to repeal law that bars opposition from office
stories.say: Venezuela's assembly speaker says the Simón Bolívar law, which bars people who backed foreign sanctions from political office, will be repealed, possibly next week.
stories.stand: Critics said the 2024 law enabled political persecution.
body: Jorge Rodríguez, speaker of Venezuela's National Assembly, said the Simón Bolívar Law will be repealed and expected the reforms to be approved the following week, Sigmalive reported.

The law, passed after the July 2024 election, permanently bars people who requested or supported foreign sanctions from political office and allows their assets to be confiscated. Rodríguez said no politician had been subjected to it.
Opposition leader María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela in October. Interim president Delcy Rodríguez's government has been negotiating with opposition parties. No election date has been set.

stories.say: Erin Patterson, jailed for life for murdering three relatives with a death cap mushroom lunch, has asked Australia's High Court to hear a final appeal.
stories.stand: Victoria's Court of Appeal rejected her bid to quash the convictions last month.
body: Erin Patterson filed an application with Australia's High Court on Friday, her final chance to appeal, Reuters reported via Yahoo News. Her lawyers argue the Court of Appeal misapplied principles of justice.
A jury found her guilty last year of murdering three relatives with a beef Wellington containing death cap mushrooms at a 2023 lunch in Leongatha, and of attempting to murder a fourth person.

Last month the Court of Appeal rejected her appeal against conviction and imposed life without parole after a prosecution appeal. Patterson maintains her innocence and says the deaths were an accident.

stories.head: DWP takes benefit and pension services offline after cyber incident
stories.say: The Department for Work and Pensions has taken some online benefit and pension services offline after a serious cyber incident. Ministers say regular payments are unaffected.
stories.stand: Unusual activity was spotted on Thursday; investigators say there is no evidence other departments were targeted.
body: The Department for Work and Pensions took some online services offline as a precaution after unusual activity was identified on Thursday, ITV News reported. They still appeared offline on Friday evening.

Online services for pensioners, Universal Credit and Personal Independence Payment applications were affected, Euronews reported. Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden called the incident serious but said regular payments were continuing as normal.

Downing Street said there was no evidence a malicious actor had targeted other departments, but did not rule out a hack. The National Cyber Security Centre is helping. The DWP makes about 2.5 million regular payments a day.

stories.head: Two PCs face misconduct hearing over assault probe before train attack
stories.say: Two Cambridgeshire police officers face a gross misconduct hearing over their handling of an assault weeks before last year's Huntingdon train stabbings.
stories.stand: The force has apologised and says missed opportunities may have prevented the attack.
body: Two Cambridgeshire Constabulary officers face a gross misconduct hearing over their handling of an alleged assault in Peterborough on 27 September 2025, ITV News reported. No date has been set.

The IOPC alleges one officer failed to make appropriate inquiries, and that both falsely claimed no CCTV was available. Assistant Chief Constable Leighton Hammett apologised and said missed opportunities may have prevented the attack.
Anthony Williams, 33, was convicted of 14 counts of attempted murder over stabbings in Peterborough, on the DLR and on an LNER train between 31 October and 1 November 2025. All the victims survived.

stories.head: RAF apologises after jets flew low over Lockerbie
stories.say: The R A F has apologised for distress caused by military jets flying low over Lockerbie, where an understanding since the 1988 bombing has been to avoid low flying.
stories.stand: Local MP David Mundell raised it in the Commons weeks before the bombing's 38th anniversary.
body: The RAF has apologised after military jets flew low over Lockerbie earlier in November, ITV News reported. Swiss Air Force F/A-18 Hornets were reportedly practising night flying alongside RAF aircraft.
After the 1988 bombing there was an understanding that low flying over the town would be avoided. Local MP David Mundell raised it in the Commons and asked to meet the Ministry of Defence.
The RAF said it was sorry for any distress, is investigating, and aims to publicise low flying in advance where possible. The Pan Am bombing killed 259 people on board and 11 on the ground.

stories.stand: The foundation, renamed the 1189808 Foundation, lodged the application at Companies House on Friday.
body: The charity set up by the family of Captain Sir Tom Moore has applied to be struck off, with an application appearing at Companies House on Friday, ITV News reported. It dropped his name last year and is now the 1189808 Foundation.
The charities watchdog found repeated misconduct and mismanagement by his daughter, Hannah Ingram-Moore, and her husband, Colin. Benefits included a £1.4 million book deal linked to the foundation.
Hannah Ingram-Moore received a 10-year ban from being a charity trustee and Colin an eight-year ban. Sir Tom raised £38 million for NHS Charities Together before he died in 2021.

stories.stand: Brand was jailed for ten and a half years for one rape and three sexual assaults.
body: Siobhan Blake, the Crown Prosecution Service's national lead for rape and serious sexual offences, said victims deal with their ordeal in "wholly different ways", ITV News reported.

The CPS says 70% of rape cases passed by police lead to a charge. The government is setting up an expert working group on rape myths.

stories.stand: The drive is backed by £874 million, and nearly 2,000 extra bed spaces have been funded.

stories.say: The Home Office has announced ninety-five million pounds to tackle violence against women and girls, most of it for programmes that work with abusers.
stories.stand: The package marks a year since the government's Freedom from Violence and Abuse Strategy.
body: The Home Office announced a £95,583,990 package on Friday, presented by safeguarding minister Satvir Kaur.

About £70.3 million goes to perpetrator programmes, including behaviour-change work for abusers. Helplines and online services, including Refuge's National Domestic Abuse Helpline, get about £18.3 million.
A fund giving cash to victims fleeing abuse gets £1,775,000; it supported 3,416 victims in 2025-26. The government's goal is to halve violence against women and girls in a decade.

No arrests have been made. Police are reviewing footage and talking to authorities investigating similar incidents at two other Don Toliver concerts in Europe.

Lead author Kevin Mulcahy suggests Victorian-era assumptions may have shaped how the fossils were first interpreted in the late 1800s.

stories.head: Men skip more questions than women while multitasking, study finds
stories.say: A small study found men and women multitasked equally well on most tasks, but men left conversational questions unanswered more than twice as often.
stories.stand: The study of 78 adults is published in Psychological Research.
body: Researchers at Brunel University London and City St George's, University of London, asked 41 men and 37 women to do five everyday-style tasks while answering questions every 20 seconds, ScienceDaily reported.
Men and women performed similarly on four of the five tasks. Men left conversational questions unanswered more than twice as often, though their answers were as fast and accurate.

stories.say: Long trenches across Australia's Nullarbor Plain turn out to be surface traces of deeply buried caves, a method researchers say could help find caves on Mars.
stories.stand: The trenches run up to 20 kilometres and were mapped with drones, satellites and boreholes.
body: Long, shallow trenches up to 20 km long on the Nullarbor Plain in southern Australia are surface traces of deeply buried cave systems that have been collapsing upwards over millions of years, ScienceDaily reported.
Researchers used drone and aerial photography, satellite landscape models, boreholes and geophysical imaging. The study is in Communications Earth & Environment.
The authors say the method could help find hidden caves holding ancient records, and could help identify possible caves on Mars.

body: Researchers at the University of Miami identified a previously unknown group of viruses with smaller, simpler genomes than related viruses, ScienceDaily reported. The study is in Nature Communications.

The team searched billions of DNA sequences using bioinformatics, protein language models and AlphaFold.

body: The UK Preclinical Translational Models Hub, a £20 million facility on the Cambridge Biomedical Campus, opened on Friday, the government said.

stories.say: The EU drugs agency says most people treated in emergency departments for drug toxicity had taken more than one substance, with cocaine involved in about a third of visits.
stories.stand: The analysis covered about 7,400 cases from 45 hospitals in 18 EU countries and Norway.
body: The European Union Drugs Agency analysed about 7,400 emergency cases from 45 hospitals in 18 EU countries and Norway in 2025, Euronews reported.

Jordan Cox hit 33 to finish the chase after rain breaks. England lead the five-match series 2-1. Jersey's Asa Tribe has been called up for the last two games, ITV News reported.

stories.head: Macron condemns violence against Bulgarian fans in Marseille
stories.say: Emmanuel Macron has condemned violence against Levski Sofia fans before their Europa League match in Marseille, where five people were taken to hospital.
stories.stand: Several hundred Marseille fans breached the away section before kick-off; Marseille won 1-0.
body: Fans clashed in the stands before Marseille's Europa League match against Levski Sofia at the Stade Velodrome on Thursday, Al Jazeera reported. Several hundred Marseille fans breached the away section, where about 500 visiting fans were.
Five people were taken to hospital and six treated on site. A police source said all the injured were Bulgarian. No arrests had been reported. Marseille won 1-0.
French President Emmanuel Macron condemned the violence, and Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova called it unacceptable and asked UEFA to examine fan safety.

stories.head: Ireland beat Australia 38-14 at Twickenham
stories.say: Ireland beat Australia thirty-eight to fourteen at Twickenham on Friday, their seventh straight win over the Wallabies, as captain Allan Alaalatoa won his hundredth cap.
stories.stand: James McNabey scored two late tries and Sam Prendergast kicked five conversions.
body: Ireland beat Australia 38-14 in the Nations Championship at Twickenham, Rugby.com.au reported. It was Ireland's seventh straight win over the Wallabies.

Robbie Henshaw, Nick Timoney and Robert Baloucoune scored tries, and James McNabey added two late. Sam Prendergast kicked five conversions and a penalty. Jeremy Williams scored the first Wallabies try.
Captain Allan Alaalatoa won his 100th Test cap. The match decided fifth place in the Nations Championship, ABC News reported.

stories.head: Cricket Australia forum to review ball management across 2017-18
stories.say: Cricket Australia's forum on the twenty eighteen ball-tampering scandal will examine the whole twenty seventeen to eighteen season, including the Ashes, overseen by barrister Fiona McLeod.
stories.stand: Participation is voluntary and the forum will make no adverse findings.
body: Cricket Australia's six-week forum, overseen by barrister Fiona McLeod, will examine ball-management practices across the 2017-18 season, including the Ashes, as well as the 2018 South Africa Tests, Al Jazeera reported.
It follows Usman Khawaja's claim that the whole team knew about the cheating in South Africa. Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood deny prior knowledge.
Participation is voluntary, and the forum will make no adverse findings. Chair David Boon said it was the best opportunity for people to be heard.

stories.stand: The opposition did not recognise him, teammates said.
body: Indian wicketkeeper-batter Rishabh Pant played for the Open House Swingers in a social Last Man Stands match at Hagley Park, Christchurch, on Wednesday, listed on the scorecard as "Stan Stan", Al Jazeera reported.

stories.head: Government backs bill to stop lawsuits used to silence scrutiny
stories.say: The government is backing Sir John Whittingdale's bill to extend protection against so-called SLAPPs, lawsuits used to silence journalists and whistleblowers, to all public interest cases.
stories.stand: Campaigners and some MPs say the bill should be strengthened.
body: Justice minister Sarah Sackman said on Friday the government will support a private member's bill from Conservative MP Sir John Whittingdale targeting SLAPPs, strategic lawsuits against public participation, Press Gazette reported.
Existing protections cover only economic crime cases. The bill would extend them to all matters of public interest, letting courts dismiss such claims early.
"No-one should be able to use their wealth or influence to silence legitimate scrutiny," Sackman said. Some MPs and the NUJ want the bill strengthened, and it must still pass further stages.

body: Within Temptation have announced Through Fire & Ashes - The 2027 Tour, 30 shows starting in Mexico City on 3 June 2027 and ending at Amsterdam's Ziggo Dome on 4 December, Blabbermouth reported.
